ev.q: During 2013–2021, annual reported measles incidence decreased by 95%, from 33.2 to 1.4 cases per million population
During 2018–2022, the discarded nonmeasles and nonrubella rate (NMNR),*** a measure of surveillance sensitivity, approximately tripled, from 1.2 to 3.3 per 100,000 population
coverage with a first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV) decreased from 87% to 84%
The percentage of cases investigated within 48 hours of notification increased from 65% in 2018 to 74% in 2022
with a reported measles incidence of 29 cases per million and a reported rubella incidence of 3 per million
the national reporting rate for suspected CRS cases (a marker of CRS surveillance sensitivity) increased 85% from 1.71 to 3.16 per 10,000 live births
MCV1 coverage decreased approximately 3%, from 87% in 2013 to 84% in 2022
achieving and maintaining ≥95% coverage with the first and second doses of measles- and rubella-containing vaccine
This report describes Indonesia’s progress toward measles and rubella elimination during 2013–2022.
During 2013–2022, measles incidence decreased from 33.2 cases per million population to a low of 1.4 in 2021
achieving and maintaining ≥95% coverage with the first and second doses of measles- and rubella-containing vaccine in every district

methods_quotes.q: Administrative vaccination coverage (the number of vaccine doses administered divided by the estimated target population) is reported each year
WHO and UNICEF use reported administrative coverage, official estimates, and vaccination coverage survey data to generate annual estimates of national immunization coverage
